project.name: CasesTD
project.description: OOP final project: a Bloons-style tower defense game with a case-opening (gacha) layer where players earn Coins from waves, unbox towers into an inventory, then place, upgrade, or sell them. Built with Java 21 Swing, Maven, MySQL, and Gson.

nodes.name: DatabaseConnection.java
nodes.summary: Lazy-initialized Singleton that loads MySQL credentials from data/db_config.properties and hands out the single shared JDBC connection, reconnecting if it was closed.
nodes.languageNotes: Classic lazy Singleton with a private constructor and static getInstance().

nodes.name: DatabaseConnection
nodes.summary: Singleton wrapper around the shared JDBC Connection configured from a properties file.

nodes.name: getInstance
nodes.summary: Returns the lazily created singleton instance.

nodes.name: getConnection
nodes.summary: Returns the open JDBC connection, reopening it via DriverManager when null or closed.

nodes.name: CaseRNGManager.java
nodes.summary: Gacha random number logic: rolls a rarity from a case's weighted odds and then picks a tower of that rarity from the case's pool.

nodes.name: CaseRNGManager
nodes.summary: Weighted random roller for case openings, injectable with a Random for testing.

nodes.name: roll
nodes.summary: Rolls a rarity for the case and picks a random tower of that rarity from its pool.

nodes.name: rollRarity
nodes.summary: Selects a rarity by weighted random draw using the case's per-rarity weights.

nodes.name: Catalog.java
nodes.summary: Immutable in-memory catalog of every tower type and case, loaded once at startup through TowerDAO and CaseDAO and indexed by tower id.

nodes.name: Catalog
nodes.summary: Holds all TowerType and CaseDef definitions loaded from the database.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Factory method loading towers and cases from the database and failing if either table is empty.

nodes.name: GameSession.java
nodes.summary: Central run state holding coins, lives, free cases, inventory copies and placed towers; enforces buying/opening cases, placement spacing, upgrade copy costs, the one-Level-5-per-type rule, and selling/refunds.

nodes.name: GameSession
nodes.summary: Owns and mutates all per-run player state and enforces the game economy rules.

nodes.name: buyCase
nodes.summary: Spends coins on a case and adds the rolled tower to the inventory.

nodes.name: openFreeCase
nodes.summary: Consumes a free starter case and adds the rolled tower to the inventory.

nodes.name: copiesOf
nodes.summary: Counts how many inventory copies of a tower type the player owns.

nodes.name: sellInventory
nodes.summary: Sells one inventory copy of a tower type for its refund value.

nodes.name: canPlaceAt
nodes.summary: Checks that a position keeps the minimum gap from every placed tower.

nodes.name: place
nodes.summary: Places a tower from inventory on the map using TowerFactory, consuming one copy.

nodes.name: upgradeBlockReason
nodes.summary: Returns a human-readable reason why a tower cannot be upgraded, or null if it can.

nodes.name: upgradeCost
nodes.summary: Returns the number of copies needed for a tower's next level.

nodes.name: upgrade
nodes.summary: Upgrades a placed tower by consuming copies, tracking the one-Level-5-per-type rule.

nodes.name: sell
nodes.summary: Removes a placed tower from the map and refunds coins.

nodes.name: UpgradeCostTable.java
nodes.summary: Static helper that looks up how many duplicate tower copies an upgrade to a given level costs for a rarity, based on GameConfig.

nodes.name: UpgradeCostTable
nodes.summary: Non-instantiable utility class computing upgrade copy costs.

nodes.name: copiesNeeded
nodes.summary: Returns the duplicate copies required to reach a level for a given rarity.

nodes.name: CaseDAO.java
nodes.summary: Data Access Object that reads the cases table and the case_towers join table, building CaseDef records with their rarity weights and tower pools.

nodes.name: CaseDAO
nodes.summary: DAO for cases and their tower pools.

nodes.name: findAll
nodes.summary: Queries all cases with their rarity weights and attaches each case's tower pool.

nodes.name: findPool
nodes.summary: Queries the case_towers table for the tower ids in a case and resolves them to TowerTypes.

nodes.name: TowerDAO.java
nodes.summary: Data Access Object that reads all rows of the towers table and maps them to TowerType records including rarity and special effect enums.

nodes.name: TowerDAO
nodes.summary: DAO for tower type definitions.

nodes.name: findAll
nodes.summary: Queries the towers table and maps every row to a TowerType record.

nodes.name: CaseDef.java
nodes.summary: Immutable record describing a purchasable case: id, name, coin cost, per-rarity drop weights and the pool of towers it can drop.

nodes.name: CaseDef
nodes.summary: Record for a case definition with weights and a tower pool.

nodes.name: weightOf
nodes.summary: Returns the case's drop weight for a given rarity.

nodes.name: Rarity.java
nodes.summary: Enum of tower rarities (Common to Legendary) carrying display name, UI color and gem count.
nodes.languageNotes: Java enum with a constructor and fields, so each constant carries its own data.

nodes.name: Rarity
nodes.summary: Rarity enum with display metadata.

nodes.name: Special.java
nodes.summary: Enum of tower special effects (none, stun, poison, burn, buff, turrets, pierce) as stored in the towers table.

nodes.name: Special
nodes.summary: Enum of tower special effect kinds.

nodes.name: TowerType.java
nodes.summary: Immutable record for one tower blueprint row: name, class, rarity, base stats, special effect parameters, description and sprite path (Type Object pattern).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Java record, giving a compact immutable data carrier with auto-generated accessors, equals and hashCode.

nodes.name: TowerType
nodes.summary: Record holding a tower blueprint's fixed stats.

nodes.name: ShopOverlay.java
nodes.summary: Swing overlay that renders the case shop over the map with three views: case cards with drop odds, an animated spinning reveal strip, and the result card; delegates the actual purchase and roll to GameSession.

nodes.name: ShopOverlay
nodes.summary: Overlay UI controller and renderer for the case shop and its opening animation.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Advances the spin animation and switches to the result view when it ends.

nodes.name: click
nodes.summary: Routes mouse clicks to close, collect, skip or case buttons depending on the current view.

nodes.name: clickCases
nodes.summary: Handles clicks on case cards and starts opening the chosen case.

nodes.name: openCase
nodes.summary: Pays for (or uses a free) case through GameSession and builds the randomized reveal strip ending on the won tower.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Draws the overlay backdrop, header and the active view.

nodes.name: paintCases
nodes.summary: Draws case cards with tower previews, drop chances and buy buttons.

nodes.name: paintStrip
nodes.summary: Draws the eased scrolling strip of tower cards during the spin.

nodes.name: paintResult
nodes.summary: Draws the won tower card with rarity, description and inventory count.

nodes.name: GameConfig.java
nodes.summary: Gson-deserialized game balance configuration (economy, wave scaling, explicit wave spawn lists) loaded from waves_config.json, with helpers for kill rewards, wave-clear rewards and per-wave enemy health/speed multipliers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses public nested static POJO classes so Gson can map JSON directly onto fields without setters.

nodes.name: GameConfig
nodes.summary: Root config object with nested Economy, Scaling, SpawnDef and WaveDef classes plus balance helper methods.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the JSON config file with Gson, throwing IllegalStateException if it cannot be read.

nodes.name: explicitWave
nodes.summary: Returns the hand-defined wave definition for a wave number, or null if not explicitly listed.

nodes.name: killReward
nodes.summary: Coins awarded for killing an enemy type, defaulting to 5.

nodes.name: waveClearReward
nodes.summary: Coins awarded for clearing a wave: base reward plus a per-wave increment.

nodes.name: healthScale
nodes.summary: Computes the enemy health multiplier for a wave using linear per-wave growth plus periodic multiplicative jumps.

nodes.name: speedScale
nodes.summary: Computes the enemy speed multiplier for a wave, capped by speedCapPercent.

nodes.name: GameMap.java
nodes.summary: Loads the enemy path polyline from a CSV file and parameterizes positions by distance along the path; also decides where towers may be built by checking clearance from the track, decorative roads and obstacles.

nodes.name: GameMap
nodes.summary: Path model storing polyline points and cumulative segment lengths for distance-based enemy positioning and build validation.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Parses the path CSV (skipping header/blank lines), scales points to the map canvas and builds a GameMap.

nodes.name: GameMap
nodes.summary: Constructor that precomputes cumulative distances along the path and its total length.

nodes.name: getTotalLength
nodes.summary: Returns the total length of the enemy path.

nodes.name: getPoints
nodes.summary: Returns the path's polyline points.

nodes.name: getExtraRoads
nodes.summary: Returns decorative and dead-end road segments scaled to map coordinates for rendering.

nodes.name: pointAt
nodes.summary: Interpolates the (x, y) position at a given distance along the path.

nodes.name: distanceToPath
nodes.summary: Returns the shortest distance from a point to any segment of the enemy path.

nodes.name: canBuildAt
nodes.summary: Checks whether a tower may be placed at a point: inside bounds and clear of the path, extra roads and obstacles.

nodes.name: RunResult.java
nodes.summary: Immutable record summarizing a finished run (waves cleared, kills, cases opened, previous best, new-record flag) passed to the results screen.
nodes.languageNotes: Java record: compact immutable data carrier with auto-generated accessors, equals and hashCode.

nodes.name: RunResult
nodes.summary: Record of end-of-run statistics shown on the results screen.

nodes.name: PlayerDAO.java
nodes.summary: Data access object for the MySQL players table: looks up profiles by name, creates profiles on first login, and conditionally updates the highest score.
nodes.languageNotes: JDBC PreparedStatements with try-with-resources; the UPDATE's WHERE clause guards against lowering a stored best score.

nodes.name: PlayerDAO
nodes.summary: DAO wrapping JDBC queries against the players table.

nodes.name: findByName
nodes.summary: Selects a player by (case-insensitive) name and returns an Optional Player.

nodes.name: findOrCreate
nodes.summary: Returns the existing player for a name or inserts a new profile and returns it.

nodes.name: updateHighestScore
nodes.summary: Updates the stored highest score only when the new waves-cleared value is higher.

nodes.name: Player.java
nodes.summary: Simple player profile model holding id, name and highest score (waves cleared).

nodes.name: Player
nodes.summary: Player entity with id, name and highest score.

nodes.name: Player
nodes.summary: Constructs a player from database fields.

nodes.name: getPlayerId
nodes.summary: Returns the player's database id.

nodes.name: getPlayerName
nodes.summary: Returns the player's name.

nodes.name: getHighestScore
nodes.summary: Returns the player's best waves-cleared score.

nodes.name: setHighestScore
nodes.summary: Updates the in-memory highest score.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Formats the player for debug output.

nodes.name: AppController.java
nodes.summary: Top-level screen controller that wires the landing, game and results panels into the main frame, lazily loads catalog/config/map data, and handles navigation between screens.

nodes.name: AppController
nodes.summary: Controller owning the three screens and the shared game data.

nodes.name: AppController
nodes.summary: Creates the landing, game and results panels with callbacks and registers them on the main frame.

nodes.name: startRun
nodes.summary: Starts a run for the logged-in player after ensuring game data is loaded, then switches to the game screen.

nodes.name: loadData
nodes.summary: Lazily loads the catalog from MySQL and the JSON config and CSV map, showing an error dialog on failure.

nodes.name: GameButton.java
nodes.summary: Image-based clickable button component with a builder for size, position and icon, plus hover tracking and drawing.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the Builder pattern via a nested static Builder class.

nodes.name: GameButton
nodes.summary: Image button with bounds, hover state and a nested Builder.

nodes.name: GameButton
nodes.summary: Builds the button from a Builder's size, position and icon.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Hit-tests whether a point lies within the button.

nodes.name: updateHover
nodes.summary: Updates hover state from the mouse position.

nodes.name: isHovered
nodes.summary: Returns whether the mouse is over the button.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Paints the button icon, enlarged slightly when hovered.

nodes.name: TowerArt.java
nodes.summary: Static helper that draws a tower icon from its sprite when available, otherwise a placeholder shape colored by tower class.

nodes.name: TowerArt
nodes.summary: Non-instantiable helper for tower icon rendering.

nodes.name: classColor
nodes.summary: Maps a tower's class to its placeholder color.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Draws a tower sprite centered in a square, falling back to a class-colored placeholder shape.

nodes.name: GamePanel.java
nodes.summary: Main gameplay screen: runs a fixed-timestep game loop (1/60 s accumulator with x1/x2/x3 speed, paused while the shop is open), handles mouse/keyboard input for placing, selecting, upgrading and selling towers, renders the map, towers, enemies, effects and HUD, and saves new high scores when the run ends.
nodes.languageNotes: Swing Timer drives tick(); a time accumulator decouples simulation steps from repaint rate. Implements SidePanel.Actions as a callback interface.

nodes.name: GamePanel
nodes.summary: Swing gameplay panel combining game loop, input handling and rendering; implements SidePanel.Actions.

nodes.name: GamePanel
nodes.summary: Sets up size, mouse listeners and ESC/SPACE key bindings.

nodes.name: startRun
nodes.summary: Initializes a new GameSession, GameEngine and ShopOverlay for the player, resets state, loads the background and starts the timer.

nodes.name: advance
nodes.summary: Advances the simulation by real time using a fixed 1/60 s step and speed multiplier, pausing while the shop is open and finishing the run after game over.

nodes.name: finishRun
nodes.summary: Stops the loop, persists a new highest score via PlayerDAO if beaten, and reports a RunResult.

nodes.name: handlePress
nodes.summary: Routes mouse presses to the shop, side panel, quit button, tower placement or selection.

nodes.name: placeAt
nodes.summary: Places the currently selected inventory tower at a map position if allowed.

nodes.name: selectInventory
nodes.summary: Toggles placement mode for an inventory tower type.

nodes.name: sellInventory
nodes.summary: Shows a popup menu to sell one inventory copy of a tower type for coins.

nodes.name: upgradeSelected
nodes.summary: Upgrades the selected tower and shows a toast on success.

nodes.name: sellSelected
nodes.summary: Sells the selected placed tower.

nodes.name: openShop
nodes.summary: Opens the case shop overlay.

nodes.name: startWave
nodes.summary: Starts the next wave when the shop is closed and announces boss waves.

nodes.name: cycleSpeed
nodes.summary: Cycles the game speed between x1, x2 and x3.

nodes.name: paintComponent
nodes.summary: Top-level render pass drawing ground, path, grid, towers, enemies, effects, HUD, side panel, shop and banners.

nodes.name: paintGround
nodes.summary: Draws the background image or a checkerboard grass fallback.

nodes.name: paintPath
nodes.summary: Draws the enemy path and extra roads when no background image is present.

nodes.name: paintPlacementGrid
nodes.summary: Draws the placement grid while in tower placement mode.

nodes.name: paintGhost
nodes.summary: Draws a translucent preview of the tower being placed with its range and validity.

nodes.name: paintTowers
nodes.summary: Draws placed towers with sprites, range circles for the selection and support-tower turrets.

nodes.name: paintEnemy
nodes.summary: Draws an enemy with sprite rotation, status-effect tints and a health bar.

nodes.name: paintEnemyCircle
nodes.summary: Fallback enemy rendering as colored circles with status indicators.

nodes.name: paintEffect
nodes.summary: Draws fading line and circle visual effects such as shots and explosions.

nodes.name: pill
nodes.summary: Draws a rounded HUD label pill.

nodes.name: paintBanners
nodes.summary: Draws toast messages and the game-over banner.

nodes.name: LandingPanel.java
nodes.summary: Landing/menu screen where the player types a name, opens a crate to load or create their profile, and can view help or start a run; drawn from image assets with absolute-positioned buttons.

nodes.name: LandingPanel
nodes.summary: Landing screen panel with name entry, crate opening, play and help buttons.

nodes.name: LandingPanel
nodes.summary: Lays out the name field and help panel and wires mouse clicks to quit, crate, play and help actions.

nodes.name: openCrate
nodes.summary: Validates the name and loads or creates the player profile via PlayerDAO, then reveals the menu.

nodes.name: getPlayer
nodes.summary: Returns the loaded player profile, or null before the crate is opened.

nodes.name: getPlayerName
nodes.summary: Returns the trimmed name typed by the player.

nodes.name: paintComponent
nodes.summary: Paints either the start or menu screen depending on state.

nodes.name: paintStartScreen
nodes.summary: Draws the start screen background, logo, name box and crate.

nodes.name: paintMenuScreen
nodes.summary: Draws the menu with player name, highest score and play/help buttons.

nodes.name: drawText
nodes.summary: Draws centered outlined text within a box.

nodes.name: DbCheck.java
nodes.summary: Read-only command-line diagnostic that verifies the database connection and PlayerDAO lookups work.

nodes.name: DbCheck
nodes.summary: Standalone database diagnostic class.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs sample PlayerDAO lookups and prints results or the failure message.

nodes.name: SpriteLoader.java
nodes.summary: Cached loader for tower sprite images by path, returning null for missing files so placeholder art is drawn instead.

nodes.name: SpriteLoader
nodes.summary: Static sprite cache keyed by file path.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns a cached image for a path, reading it from disk on first request; null if missing or unreadable.

nodes.name: Main.java
nodes.summary: Application entry point that, on the Swing event thread, creates the MainFrame window, wires up the AppController screen router, and shows the window.

nodes.name: MainFrame.java
nodes.summary: Fixed-size JFrame window that hosts all game screens in a CardLayout panel sized by Theme and exposes methods to register and switch screens by name.

nodes.name: Gfx.java
nodes.summary: Static Graphics2D text-drawing helpers for centered text, outlined (stroked) text, and word-wrapping strings to a maximum width, shared by the game UI screens.

nodes.name: TextButton.java
nodes.summary: Lightweight custom-painted button (not a Swing component) with bounds, hover and enabled state, drawn as a rounded colored box with outlined label text using Palette styling.

nodes.name: HelpPanel.java
nodes.summary: How-to-Play overlay panel that displays help book image spreads with previous/next arrow buttons and an invisible close hit area, manually laid out relative to the book and swallowing clicks to the game beneath.

nodes.name: ResultsPanel.java
nodes.summary: End-of-run results screen that paints the menu background, the player's RunResult statistics, and PLAY AGAIN / MENU TextButtons that invoke callbacks supplied by the controller.

nodes.name: SidePanel.java
nodes.summary: In-game right-hand sidebar that paints the tower inventory cards, selected-tower or placement info, and shop/start-wave/speed/upgrade/sell buttons, routing clicks through an Actions callback interface implemented by GamePanel.

nodes.name: Palette.java
nodes.summary: Shared color constants for the game visuals (grass, path, panels, cream, good/bad, gold) plus heading and body font helpers backed by FontLoader.

nodes.name: Theme.java
nodes.summary: Global UI constants defining the content window dimensions, core colors, and title/button fonts loaded via FontLoader.

nodes.name: FontLoader.java
nodes.summary: Loads the Luckiest Guy TrueType font from assets/fonts once at class init, falling back to SansSerif, and derives sized copies on request.

nodes.name: ImageLoader.java
nodes.summary: Loads UI images from assets/ui via ImageIO, returning null and logging to stderr when a file cannot be read.

nodes.name: Main
nodes.summary: Entry-point class holding the static main method that launches the Swing UI.

nodes.name: MainFrame
nodes.summary: JFrame subclass managing a CardLayout of named game screens.

nodes.name: Gfx
nodes.summary: Non-instantiable utility class of static text rendering helpers.

nodes.name: TextButton
nodes.summary: Custom-drawn clickable button with hover and enabled state, hit-tested manually by its owning panel.

nodes.name: HelpPanel
nodes.summary: JPanel overlay paging through help book spreads with arrow and close buttons.

nodes.name: ResultsPanel
nodes.summary: JPanel showing the end-of-run summary with play-again and menu actions.

nodes.name: SidePanel
nodes.summary: Sidebar renderer and click router bound to the current GameSession and GameEngine, delegating player actions via its nested Actions interface.

nodes.name: Palette
nodes.summary: Constant holder for game colors and font helper methods.

nodes.name: Theme
nodes.summary: Constant holder for window size, base colors, and fonts.

nodes.name: FontLoader
nodes.summary: Final utility class caching the base UI font and deriving sizes.

nodes.name: ImageLoader
nodes.summary: Final utility class for loading UI images from disk.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Schedules creation of MainFrame and AppController on the Swing event dispatch thread and shows the window.

nodes.name: showScreen
nodes.summary: Switches the visible CardLayout card to a previously registered screen name.

nodes.name: addScreen
nodes.summary: Registers a JPanel under a screen name in the card layout.

nodes.name: wrap
nodes.summary: Splits text into lines that fit a maximum pixel width using font metrics.

nodes.name: outlined
nodes.summary: Draws text with a dark stroked outline by rendering the glyph shape's stroke and fill.

nodes.name: centered
nodes.summary: Draws text horizontally centered on a given x coordinate.

nodes.name: outlinedCentered
nodes.summary: Draws outlined text centered on a given x coordinate.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Paints the button's rounded body, hover highlight or disabled dimming, and outlined centered label.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Hit-tests a point against the button bounds.

nodes.name: updateHover
nodes.summary: Updates hover state from the current mouse position.

nodes.name: bookBounds
nodes.summary: Computes the scaled, centered rectangle where the help book image is drawn.

nodes.name: doLayout
nodes.summary: Positions the arrow and close buttons relative to the current book bounds.

nodes.name: paintComponent
nodes.summary: Dims the background and draws the current help spread image or a placeholder.

nodes.name: showSpread
nodes.summary: Clamps and switches to a spread index, toggling arrow visibility.

nodes.name: paintComponent
nodes.summary: Paints the background, result title, player name, run statistics, and the two action buttons.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Stores the RunResult and player name to display and triggers a repaint.

nodes.name: click
nodes.summary: Routes left/right clicks to inventory cards or sidebar buttons, invoking the matching Actions callback.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Paints the sidebar background, coin/lives/wave stats, inventory, info section, and control buttons.

nodes.name: paintInventory
nodes.summary: Lays out and draws inventory cards for each owned tower type with art and copy counts.

nodes.name: paintInfo
nodes.summary: Chooses between selected-tower, placement, or default help info for the info section.

nodes.name: paintTowerInfo
nodes.summary: Draws the selected tower's level, stats, passive description, and upgrade/sell buttons with costs or block reasons.

nodes.name: paintPlacingInfo
nodes.summary: Draws info about the tower type currently being placed.

nodes.name: bind
nodes.summary: Attaches a new GameSession and GameEngine and resets selection, placement, and speed state.

nodes.name: heading
nodes.summary: Returns the shared heading font at a given size.

nodes.name: body
nodes.summary: Returns the shared body font at a given size.

nodes.name: getFont
nodes.summary: Returns the cached base font derived to the requested point size.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads an image from assets/ui, returning null on I/O failure.

nodes.name: GameEngine.java
nodes.summary: Core game-loop logic that runs waves, recomputes tower buffs, fires towers, moves enemies, pays kill and wave-clear rewards, and detects game over.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a nested enum State as a small finite-state machine (BETWEEN_WAVES, WAVE_ACTIVE, GAME_OVER) and Iterator.remove() for safe in-loop deletion.

nodes.name: GameEngine
nodes.summary: Central simulation driver owning the live enemy and effect lists, a WaveSpawner, and the wave/kill counters exposed to the UI.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Per-frame tick: ages effects, spawns enemies, resets then reapplies tower auras (max not sum), updates towers and enemies, handles kills, leaks, game over and wave-clear rewards.

nodes.name: updateEffects
nodes.summary: Advances every VisualEffect and removes the ones that have finished.

nodes.name: startNextWave
nodes.summary: Begins the next wave via the WaveSpawner when the engine is between waves; returns false otherwise.

nodes.name: VisualEffect.java
nodes.summary: Immutable-shape, time-limited visual effect (shot line or blast circle) with fade-out, produced by towers and drawn by the game panel.
nodes.languageNotes: Static factory methods line() and circle() hide the overloaded meaning of the coordinate fields behind a private constructor.

nodes.name: VisualEffect
nodes.summary: Short-lived line or circle effect with color, duration and remaining time; exposes a fade factor for rendering.

nodes.name: VisualEffect
nodes.summary: Private constructor storing kind, coordinates, color and duration for a new effect.

nodes.name: TowerFactory.java
nodes.summary: Factory that maps a TowerType's database tower_class string to the matching concrete Tower subclass.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Java switch expression with arrow cases and a private constructor to make a non-instantiable static factory.

nodes.name: TowerFactory
nodes.summary: Non-instantiable static factory producing SingleTarget, Splash, Sniper or Support towers from a TowerType.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Instantiates the Tower subclass named by type.towerClass() at the given position, throwing on unknown names.

nodes.name: Enemy.java
nodes.summary: Abstract zombie base class handling path movement, health, rewards, and status effects (stun with immunity window, poison, stacking burn).
nodes.languageNotes: takeDamage delegates to a protected reduceDamage hook so subclasses like ArmoredEnemy can soften hits without overriding the core damage path.

nodes.name: Enemy
nodes.summary: Abstract enemy implementing Damageable; tracks track distance, position, facing angle, and stun/poison/burn timers.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Applies poison and burn damage over time, advances stun and immunity timers, moves along the track and updates position and facing angle.

nodes.name: takeDamage
nodes.summary: Subtracts damage after passing it through the reduceDamage hook.

nodes.name: reduceDamage
nodes.summary: Overridable hook returning the damage actually taken; identity by default.

nodes.name: stun
nodes.summary: Stuns the enemy for the given seconds if it is not already stunned or immune; returns whether it landed.

nodes.name: canBeStunned
nodes.summary: Reports whether a stun would land now (alive, not stunned, not in immunity window).

nodes.name: burn
nodes.summary: Adds a burn stack (capped at 5) and refreshes burn duration.

nodes.name: poison
nodes.summary: Applies poison keeping the strongest DPS and longest duration.

nodes.name: SingleTargetTower.java
nodes.summary: Basic tower that shoots the enemy furthest along the track; its Level 5 passive makes it fire 50% faster.

nodes.name: SingleTargetTower
nodes.summary: Single-target Tower subclass using furthestInRange targeting and a line shot effect.

nodes.name: attack
nodes.summary: Hits the furthest-along enemy in range and adds a yellow shot line; returns false when no target.

nodes.name: SniperTower.java
nodes.summary: Sniper tower that targets the highest-health enemy in range, optionally firing a piercing beam that hits multiple enemies along a line.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Java streams (filter/sorted/limit/toList) with vector projection math to find enemies on the beam.

nodes.name: SniperTower
nodes.summary: Tower subclass targeting the healthiest enemy; PIERCE special fires a beam via projection math.

nodes.name: attack
nodes.summary: Selects the highest-health enemy in range, then pierces or deals a single hit with a line effect.

nodes.name: pierce
nodes.summary: Casts a range-length beam through the target and damages up to effectValue enemies nearest along it.

nodes.name: SplashTower.java
nodes.summary: Area-damage tower that blasts the furthest enemy and everything within its splash radius, applying poison or burn depending on its special.

nodes.name: SplashTower
nodes.summary: Splash Tower subclass dealing radius damage and applying POISON or BURN status effects.

nodes.name: attack
nodes.summary: Damages all enemies within the splash radius of the furthest target and adds a colored blast circle.

nodes.name: SupportTower.java
nodes.summary: Multi-role support tower whose special selects behavior: STUN (Policeman stuns everything in range), TURRETS (mini-turrets each hit a different enemy), or BUFF (fire-rate aura for nearby towers).
nodes.languageNotes: Dispatches behavior with a switch expression on an enum, and overrides getDamage/getFireRate to opt the STUN variant out of level scaling.

nodes.name: SupportTower
nodes.summary: Tower subclass covering stun, mini-turret and aura-buff support variants.

nodes.name: attack
nodes.summary: Dispatches to stunAll or fireTurrets based on the tower's special; BUFF towers never fire.

nodes.name: stunAll

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: CasesTD is a Bloons-style tower defense game with a case-opening (gacha) layer: you earn Coins by clearing zombie waves, open cases to unbox towers into an inventory, then place, upgrade, or sell them. The README covers setup (JDK 21, Maven, MySQL 8, running schema.sql and seed_data.sql, copying the DB config) and GAME_GUIDE.md is the defense guide that maps the layered architecture and shows where each OOP concept lives. Read both first, because the rest of the tour follows the same layers: database, domain model, game core, and Swing UI.

tour.title: Build and Entry Point
tour.description: pom.xml is the Maven build for Java 21, and it pulls in MySQL Connector/J and Gson, the two libraries the persistence and config layers use. Main.java is the entry point. On the Swing event thread it creates the fixed-size MainFrame (a CardLayout that hosts every screen) and wires in AppController, which switches between the landing, game, and results screens. The BFS dependency walk starts here, and every other class is reached through AppController.
tour.languageLesson: Swing is not thread-safe, so the UI must be built on the Event Dispatch Thread. SwingUtilities.invokeLater(() -> ...) schedules the lambda on the EDT. CardLayout stacks several panels in one container and shows one at a time, which is a simple way to build screen navigation.

tour.title: Database Schema and Seed Data
tour.description: The MySQL schema splits the data into two groups. The rebuildable catalog tables are towers (class, rarity, damage, range, fire rate, special effect), cases (cost plus per-rarity drop weights constrained to sum to 100), and the case_towers join table that defines each case's drop pool. The players table is persistent and stores each profile's best score. seed_data.sql fills in the starting tower catalog and the Standard/Premium/Legendary cases, so balancing is data-driven: tower and case stats live in the database, not in Java code.
tour.languageLesson: case_towers is a classic many-to-many join table: one case can drop many towers, and one tower can appear in many cases. Its foreign keys use ON DELETE CASCADE so join rows are removed with their parent. A CHECK constraint (weights summing to 100) enforces a business rule in the database itself.

tour.title: Singleton Database Connection
tour.description: DatabaseConnection is the project's Singleton: a lazily created single instance reads the JDBC URL, user, and password from data/db_config.properties (git-ignored, copied from the example template) and hands out the one shared connection. Keeping credentials in a properties file keeps secrets out of source control, and the Singleton gives every DAO in the next step the same access point.
tour.languageLesson: Singleton pattern in Java: a private constructor stops outside code from calling new, a private static field holds the one instance, and a public static getInstance() creates it on first use (lazy initialization). Be ready to explain the trade-off: it is a global access point, which is convenient but makes testing harder.

tour.title: DAO Layer
tour.description: The DAO (Data Access Object) pattern keeps all SQL in the dao package. TowerDAO maps rows of the towers table to TowerType records, CaseDAO joins cases with case_towers to build CaseDef records, and PlayerDAO looks up, creates, and updates Player profiles and their high scores. The rest of the game never sees SQL or JDBC. It works with plain Java objects, which is a clear example of separation of concerns.
tour.languageLesson: JDBC basics: get a Connection, build a PreparedStatement (the ? placeholders prevent SQL injection), and iterate a ResultSet with rs.next(). try-with-resources (try (var ps = ...) { }) closes statements and result sets automatically, even when an exception is thrown.

tour.title: Type Object: Blueprints and Catalog
tour.description: TowerType is the single most depended-on file (highest fan-in). It is an immutable blueprint for one tower row: name, class, Rarity, base stats, and Special effect. It is not a tower on the map. That is the Type Object pattern: many placed Tower objects (Step 7) can share one TowerType. CaseDef plays the same role for cases, and Catalog loads every TowerType and CaseDef once at startup through the DAOs and keeps them in memory, so gameplay never queries the database.
tour.languageLesson: Java records (record TowerType(String name, ...)) are concise immutable data carriers: the compiler generates the constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode, and toString. Java enums like Rarity can hold fields and constructors (display name, color, gem count), so they are full classes with a fixed set of instances.

tour.title: Tower: Template Method and Interfaces
tour.description: Tower is the abstract base of every placed tower and implements the Template Method pattern. Its final update() handles cooldown timing and then calls the abstract attack() hook that each subclass must provide, so the overall algorithm is fixed and only the targeting and damage step varies. Tower also implements the Upgradable interface (level reads and level-ups), and UpgradeCostTable says how many duplicate copies an upgrade costs for each rarity, which ties the gacha inventory into upgrades.
tour.languageLesson: Declaring update() as final stops subclasses from overriding the skeleton. Declaring attack() as abstract forces them to fill in the step. Abstract class vs interface: Tower holds shared state and code (abstract class), while Upgradable is only a contract (interface). A class can extend one class but implement many interfaces.

tour.title: Tower Subclasses and Polymorphism
tour.description: Each concrete tower overrides the attack() hook from Step 7 differently. SingleTargetTower shoots the enemy furthest along the track, SniperTower picks the highest-health enemy and can fire a piercing beam, SplashTower deals area damage with poison or burn, and SupportTower changes behavior based on its Special (stun, turrets, buffs). The engine just calls tower.update() on a list of Tower references, and dynamic dispatch runs the right subclass code. That is runtime polymorphism.
tour.languageLesson: @Override asks the compiler to check that a method really overrides a superclass method. Polymorphism means the declared type (Tower) decides which methods you can call, and the runtime object type (SniperTower) decides which implementation runs.

tour.title: Enemy Hierarchy and Hooks
tour.description: Enemy is the abstract zombie base class and implements the Damageable interface. It handles movement along the path, health, rewards, and status effects such as stun with immunity windows. Subclasses specialize through overriding: ArmoredEnemy overrides the reduceDamage hook to take 30% less damage, BossEnemy (every 10th wave) halves any stun applied to it, and FastEnemy trades health for speed. Towers from Step 8 only ever talk to the Enemy/Damageable type, so new zombie kinds need no tower changes.
tour.languageLesson: A protected hook method like reduceDamage(double dmg) gives subclasses one specific point to change behavior without copying the base class's takeDamage logic. Overriding it in ArmoredEnemy is a small, clear polymorphism example to show a professor. The base class calls the hook, the subclass decides the result.

tour.title: Factory Pattern
tour.description: TowerFactory maps a TowerType's tower_class string from the database to the matching concrete Tower subclass. EnemyFactory turns an enemy type name into the right Enemy subclass and applies the wave's health and speed scaling. Callers ask for a tower or enemy by data, never by calling new SniperTower(...) directly, so object creation lives in one place. This is how database rows (Step 3) become polymorphic objects (Steps 8 and 9).
tour.languageLesson: A Java switch expression (switch (cls) { case "SNIPER" -> new SniperTower(type); ... default -> throw ...; }) is a clean way to write a simple factory. The return type is the abstract base class, so callers depend on the abstraction, not on concrete classes.

tour.title: Map Path and Distance Movement
tour.description: GameMap loads the zombie path from map1_path.csv as a polyline of x,y corner points and describes positions by distance traveled along the path, not by raw coordinates. An enemy only stores how far it has walked, and GameMap converts that distance into a screen point by finding the right segment and interpolating within it. It also decides where towers may be placed. The same distance value lets towers find the enemy furthest along the track.
tour.languageLesson: Linear interpolation: for a segment from A to B of length len, a point at distance d into it is A + (B - A) * (d / len). Precomputing cumulative segment lengths turns 'where is distance X?' into a quick lookup.

tour.title: Waves and Game Balance Config
tour.description: waves_config.json holds all the tuning numbers: starting coins and lives, wave rewards, kill coins, sell refunds, wave scaling, and explicit spawn lists for the early waves. GameConfig is the Gson-deserialized Java view of that file. WaveSpawner uses it to build a time-stamped spawn queue for each wave, falling back to a formula for later waves and adding a boss every 10th wave, and EnemyFactory (Step 10) creates the actual enemies. Designers can rebalance the game without recompiling.
tour.languageLesson: Gson maps JSON to Java objects by reflection: new Gson().fromJson(reader, GameConfig.class) fills fields whose names match the JSON keys, including nested objects and lists. A spawn queue sorted by timestamp lets the engine release each enemy once elapsed time passes its spawn time.

tour.title: Game Engine and Fixed-Timestep Loop
tour.description: GamePanel is the main gameplay screen and the widest-reaching file (highest fan-out). It runs a fixed-timestep loop: a time accumulator advances the simulation in exact 1/60 s steps, multiplied for the x1/x2/x3 speed buttons and paused while the shop is open. Each tick calls GameEngine, which runs the wave, recomputes tower buffs, fires towers, moves enemies, and pays kill and wave rewards. VisualEffect objects (shot lines, blast circles) fade out over time. Keeping the simulation in GameEngine and the drawing in GamePanel separates model from view.
tour.languageLesson: Fixed timestep: accumulator += frameTime; while (accumulator >= DT) { update(DT); accumulator -= DT; } then repaint(). Physics stays deterministic no matter how fast frames render. In Swing, drawing goes in an overridden paintComponent(Graphics g), and you trigger it with repaint(), never by calling paint directly.

tour.title: Session Economy and Gacha RNG
tour.description: GameSession holds the state for one run (coins, lives, free cases, inventory copies, placed towers) and is the project's clearest encapsulation example. Fields are private, and the only way to change them is through methods that enforce the rules, such as being unable to buy a case without enough coins or upgrade without enough copies. CaseRNGManager does the gacha roll: it first picks a rarity from the case's weighted odds, then picks a tower of that rarity from the case's pool. ShopOverlay is the UI on top, showing case cards with drop odds and the unboxing animation.
tour.languageLesson: Weighted random choice: draw r = random.nextInt(totalWeight), then walk the options subtracting each weight until r < weight. With weights summing to 100, each weight is the percentage chance. Encapsulation means methods like trySpendCoins(int) return success or failure instead of exposing a public setter, so invalid states cannot happen.

tour.title: Screens and Run Lifecycle
tour.description: The remaining screens complete the player's journey that AppController (Step 2) manages. LandingPanel takes the player name and loads or creates the profile through PlayerDAO, SidePanel shows inventory cards and selected-tower info during play, and ResultsPanel shows the immutable RunResult (waves cleared, kills, cases opened, new-record flag) before PLAY AGAIN. That full loop (login, play, unbox, results, save high score) uses every layer of the tour, so it is a good way to finish a demo.
